return (a, b, c)\n                b -= 1\n        c -= 1\n    b = int(num_ranks**(1/2.))\n    while b > 1:\n        if num_ranks % b == 0: a = num_ranks // b; return (a, b, 1)\n        b -= 1\n    return (num_ranks, 1, 1)\n\ndef _suggest_problem_size_from_dofs(total_dofs: int) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:\n    \"\"\"Creates a balanced 3D problem size from a total DOF count.\"\"\"\n    side = int(total_dofs**(1/3.))\n    return (side, side, side)\n\ndef _build_command_string(base_command: str, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Builds the full command string from a base and parameter dictionary.\"\"\"\n    problem = params['problem_size']\n    topo = params['topology']\n    problem_args = f\"-P {problem[0]} {problem[1]} {problem[2]}\"\n    topo_args = f\"-n {topo[0]} {topo[1]} {topo[2]}\"\n    return f\"{base_command} {problem_args} {topo_args}\"\n\nDecision = Literal[\"RETRY\", \"STOP\"]\nProblemSize = Tuple[int, int, int]\nTopology = Tuple[int, int, int]\n\ndef optimize_amg(\n    problem_size: ProblemSize,\n    topology: Topology,\n    total_instance_cpu: int,\n    total_instance_memory_gb: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    executable_command: str,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 4.5e8,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 1.0e6,\n    retry_scale_factor: float = 1.5,\n    dofs_per_gb: float = 1.2e7,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.95\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Acts as an optimizer for a single-node run, suggesting new parameters\n    and a full execution command. The only STOP condition is meeting the\n    performance threshold or being unable to improve.\n\n    Args:\n        problem_size (tuple): The dimensions of the 3D problem grid that was just run (e.g., Px, Py, Pz).\n        topology (tuple): The 3D process topology of the MPI ranks used for the run (e.g., nx, ny, nz).\n        total_instance_cpu (int): The total number of physical CPU cores available in the entire instance.\n        total_instance_memory_gb (int): The total amount of system RAM, in Gigabytes, available in the entire instance.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the level of SMT/Hyper-Threading to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured \"Figure of Merit\" (FOM) from the completed run.\n        executable_command (str): The base command string for the AMG executable, excluding problem size and topology.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum FOM. Defaults to 0.90.\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A hardware-specific tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core. Defaults to 4.5e8.\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant modeling communication overhead (DOFs/rank for ~76% efficiency). Defaults to 1.0e6.\n        retry_scale_factor (float): The multiplier used to increase problem dimensions on a RETRY. Defaults to 1.5.\n        dofs_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (DOFs that fit in 1 GB of RAM). Defaults to 1.2e7.\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (e.g., only use 95% of available RAM). Defaults to 0.95.\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', and 'resources'.\n    \"\"\"\n    px, py, pz = problem_size\n    nx, ny, nz = topology\n    total_dofs = px * py * pz\n    total_ranks = nx * ny * nz\n    max_ranks_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    num_nodes_in_instance = total_instance_cpu / cores_per_node\n    memory_gb_on_node = total_instance_memory_gb / num_nodes_in_instance\n\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        next_params = {\"problem_size\": problem_size, \"topology\": (1,1,1)}\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"Topology cannot be zero.\",\n            \"resources\": {\"size\": 1, \"tasks\": 1, \"command\": _build_command_string(executable_command, next_params), \"threads\": threading_hint}\n        }\n\n    if total_ranks > max_ranks_on_node:\n        suggested_topology = _suggest_balanced_topology(max_ranks_on_node)\n        next_params = {\"problem_size\": problem_size, \"topology\": suggested_topology}\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": f\"Topology of {total_ranks} tasks exceeds the single-node limit of {max_ranks_on_node}. Suggesting smaller topology.\",\n            \"resources\": {\"size\": 1, \"tasks\": max_ranks_on_node, \"command\": _build_command_string(executable_command, next_params), \"threads\": threading_hint}\n        }\n\n    max_dofs = memory_gb_on_node * dofs_per_gb * memory_safety_factor\n    if total_dofs > max_dofs:\n        suggested_problem_size = _suggest_problem_size_from_dofs(max_dofs)\n        next_params = {\"problem_size\": suggested_problem_size, \"topology\": topology}\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": f\"Memory constraint violated. Suggesting smaller problem size to fit on one node.\",\n            \"resources\": {\"size\": 1, \"tasks\": total_ranks, \"command\": _build_command_string(executable_command, next_params), \"threads\": threading_hint}\n        }\n\n    cpu_per_rank = max_ranks_on_node // total_ranks\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cpu_per_rank\n    dofs_per_rank = total_dofs / total_ranks\n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(dofs_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    if theoretical_max_fom < 1e-9:\n        return {\"decision\": \"STOP\", \"reason\": \"Theoretical max FOM is zero.\", \"resources\": None}\n    \n    performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\", \"reason\": f\"Current FOM {current_fom:.2e} is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max {theoretical_max_fom:.2e}. Threshold met.\",\n            \"resources\": None\n        }\n\n    next_problem_size = (int(px * retry_scale_factor), int(py * retry_scale_factor), int(pz * retry_scale_factor))\n    next_total_dofs = next_problem_size[0] * next_problem_size[1] * next_problem_size[2]\n\n    if next_total_dofs > max_dofs:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\", \"reason\": f\"Performance {performance_ratio:.1%} is below threshold, but next larger problem exceeds single-node memory. Best achievable performance found.\",\n            \"resources\": None\n        }\n    next_params = {\"problem_size\": next_problem_size, \"topology\": topology}\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": f\"Performance {performance_ratio:.1%} is below threshold. Suggesting larger problem size.\",\n        \"resources\": {\"size\": 1, \"tasks\": total_ranks, \"command\": _build_command_string(executable_command, next_params), \"threads\": threading_hint}\n    }\n"

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, widely-used choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to allow for non-interactive package installations.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Update the package repository and install all necessary build and runtime dependencies.
# - build-essential: Provides core compilation tools like make, gcc, g++.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https).
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: The MPI implementation and development headers.
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library, a specific requirement.
# All actions are combined into a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
# The apt cache is cleaned up in the same layer to prevent it from being stored in the final image.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure proper operation when running as the root user and over standard TCP/IP networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Clone the latest branch of the AMG source code, compile it, and clean up.
# The executable is built using the provided Makefile which uses mpicc.
# The final 'amg' executable is copied to /usr/local/bin, making it available in the system's PATH.
# The source code directory is removed to minimize the final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg_src && \
    cd /tmp/amg_src/test && \
    make amg && \
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg_src

# Set the default command for the container to the application executable.
# This allows the container to be run simply as 'docker run <image_name>' to execute the benchmark.
CMD ["amg"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, widely-used choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to allow for non-interactive package installations.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Update the package repository and install all necessary build and runtime dependencies.
# - build-essential: Provides core compilation tools like make, gcc, g++.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https).
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: The MPI implementation and development headers.
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library, a specific requirement.
# All actions are combined into a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
# The apt cache is cleaned up in the same layer to prevent it from being stored in the final image.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure proper operation when running as the root user and over standard TCP/IP networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Clone the latest branch of the AMG source code, compile it, and clean up.
# FIX: The build is performed from the top-level directory to first build the required libraries ('make libs')
# before building the main executable ('make amg'), resolving linker errors.
# The final 'amg' executable is copied from its build location in 'test/' to /usr/local/bin.
# The source code directory is removed to minimize the final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg_src && \
    cd /tmp/amg_src && \
    make libs && \
    make amg && \
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg_src

# Set the default command for the container to the application executable.
# This allows the container to be run simply as 'docker run <image_name>' to execute the benchmark.
CMD ["amg"]

# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, widely-used choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to allow for non-interactive package installations.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Update the package repository and install all necessary build and runtime dependencies.
# - build-essential: Provides core compilation tools like make, gcc, g++.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https).
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: The MPI implementation and development headers.
# - libgomp1: Provides the GNU OpenMP runtime library, a specific requirement.
# All actions are combined into a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
# The apt cache is cleaned up in the same layer to prevent it from being stored in the final image.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure proper operation when running as the root user and over standard TCP/IP networks.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Clone the AMG source code, compile it using the default make target, and clean up.
# FIX: The build process is simplified to a single 'make' command, which uses the Makefile's default
# rule to correctly build the application. The previous 'make libs' target was invalid.
# The final 'amg' executable is copied from its build location to /usr/local/bin to be on the PATH.
# The source code directory is removed to minimize the final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /tmp/amg_src && \
    cd /tmp/amg_src && \
    make && \
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/amg_src

# Set the default command for the container to the application executable.
# This allows the container to be run simply as 'docker run <image_name>' to execute the benchmark.
CMD ["amg"]

Assets for minicluster Agent
flux-minicluster-manifest
# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves the shared library error
# by installing the missing dependency before the main application runs.
# It also incorporates performance tuning suggestions from the failure analysis,
# such as selecting a specific instance type and setting task count to match CPU cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg2023-experiment
  # Deploys to the 'default' namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # We are running on a single, larger node as suggested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, matching the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 24

  # Keep pods after the job finishes for debugging purposes.
  cleanup: false

  # Enforce strict validation of the spec.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Select a specific AWS instance type for this job, as suggested by the analysis.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # This is the application container, not the launcher. Must be false.
      launcher: false

      # The command to execute with 'flux run'.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size (4x4x4 grid).
      command: "amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4"

      # Pre-command hook to fix the execution environment.
      # The original error was a missing libgomp.so.1. This command installs it.
      commands:
        pre: "apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libgomp1"

      # Environment variables for performance tuning, as suggested by the analysis.
      environment:
        # Disable OpenMP threading since we are running one MPI rank per core.
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        # Optimize intra-node communication for shared memory.
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"

# Corrected the number of tasks to match the available CPUs on the selected node type.
# The r6a.12xlarge instance has 24 CPUs, but the job was requesting 32 tasks,
# which violates the non-oversubscription constraint and caused a Flux allocation error.
# - Changed 'tasks' from 32 to 24.
# - Updated the process topology in the command from '-n 8 4 1' (32 ranks) to '-n 6 4 1' (24 ranks).
# - Removed the redundant 'pre' command, as libgomp1 is already in the container image.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -P 192 192 192 -n 6 4 1
    environment:
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    quiet: true
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  # Set the size to 1 to ensure the job runs on a single node as requested.
  size: 1
  # Corrected tasks to 24 to match the vCPU count of the r6a.12xlarge instance.
  tasks: 24

# Corrected the amg command by swapping the arguments for the problem size (-n)
# and the processor topology (-P). The previous manifest had them reversed,
# causing the application to fail with an "Invalid number of processors" error.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  # The -n flag specifies the problem size per processor, and -P specifies the processor grid topology.
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 192 192 192 -P 6 4 1
    environment:
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    quiet: true
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  # The job runs on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks (24) matches the CPU count of the r6a.12xlarge instance
  # and the product of the processor topology (6*4*1).
  tasks: 24

      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge

# FIX: Reduced the number of tasks from 32 to 24 to match the number of available
# CPU cores on the selected r6a.12xlarge instance type. This corrects the
# oversubscription issue that caused the job to fail.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run as a single pod.
  size: 1
  # Corrected the number of tasks to 24.
  tasks: 24
  # Ensure the pod and its resources are not deleted after the job finishes
  # to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    # Reduce log verbosity for cleaner output.
    quiet: true
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Schedule the job on a specific AWS instance type.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # FIX: Updated the MPI process topology (-n flag) to match the corrected task
      # count (6 * 4 * 1 = 24).
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 432 432 432 -n 6 4 1
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
      launcher: false
      environment:
        # Optimization: Force one thread per MPI rank to maximize performance.
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
        # Optimization: Set the shared-memory communication mechanism to 'cma'
        # for better performance on modern kernels.
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma

# Error Analysis: The previous job failed with reason: OOMKilled (exit code 137).
# This indicates the application tried to allocate more memory than was available on the node.
# The primary cause is the problem size (-n 360 360 360), which was too large for the memory of the r6a.12xlarge instance.
#
# Fix: The problem size specified in the command argument is reduced from '360 360 360' to '288 288 288'.
# This smaller problem size has a significantly lower memory footprint and is expected to prevent the OOM error.
# The node selector and task count remain the same, as they are correctly configured for the instance type.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false

# The previous run failed with an Out-Of-Memory (OOMKilled) error, even after
# reducing the problem size.
# This manifest further reduces the problem size from '-n 288 288 288' to
# '-n 192 192 192' to ensure the application fits within the node's memory.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 192 192 192 -P 6 4 1
    environment:
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  logging:
    quiet: true
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 24
